question:
Which of the following substances is in solid form in the given reaction?

Sodium sulphate + barium chloride → sodium chloride + barium sulphate
solution:
The correct answer is __**Barium sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Barium sulphate is the product that forms as a precipitate in the reaction between sodium sulphate and barium chloride.
 
• It is an insoluble compound in water, leading to its solid formation in the reaction mixture.
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → 2 NaCl + BaSO₄.
 
• In this reaction, barium sulphate (BaSO₄) is the only substance that precipitates out, i.e., forms a solid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation Reaction**

 
 
• A precipitation reaction occurs when two soluble salts react in aqueous solution to form one or more insoluble products (precipitates).
 
• Barium sulphate is a common precipitate used in laboratory experiments to demonstrate precipitation reactions.
 
 
 
• **Solubility Rules**
 
 
• Solubility rules help predict whether a substance will dissolve or form a precipitate in water.
 
• Sulphates are generally soluble, except for those of barium, lead, and calcium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Barium Sulphate**
 
 
• It is used as a radiopaque agent in medical imaging of the digestive system.
 
• It is also used in the manufacturing of paints, coatings, and plastics as a white pigment and filler.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Equation Balancing**
 
 
• Balancing chemical equations ensures the conservation of mass where the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• This reaction is balanced with the formula: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → 2 NaCl + BaSO₄.
